Name: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Durayd al-Azdī
Arabic Name: محمد بن الحسن ابن دريد الأزدي
Library of Congress Name: Ibn Durayd, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, 837 or 838-933
Documentation: GAL I 111; II 14; S I 173.  Some confusion may exist in cataloguing two works attributed to Ibn Durayd: his work on morphology, المقصور والممدود, and his qasida in eulogy to al-Shāh ʾAbd-Allāh Ibn Muḥammad Ibn Mīkāl and his son Abual-Abbas Ismail, المقصورة, also known as الدريدية in West Africa and a poem widely used in the study of Arabic prosody, e.g. maqāmāt / rhyme.  Both works have correctly been identified as aids in the study of Arabic, but the second has been described in WAAMD records by its original intent as a eulogy.  Additional confusion appears between Ibn Malikʾs تحفة المودود في معرفة المقصور والممدود and Ibn Duraydʾs al-Maqsur wa al-mamdud, both on morphology.

Name: Ibn ʿAbbās
Documentation: Three authors in WAAMD are known by the nickname Ibn ʿAbbās or Abū al-ʿAbbās and have written on hadith: authors # 1343, #1272 and #4155.

Name: Ibn ʿĀṣam, Abū Bakr al-Ḥaṭṭāb
Documentation: Original cataloguing attributed this work to two author nicknames, Ibn ʿĀṣim (author # 3539) and Ḥaṭṭāb (authors # 574, 2958, 3473 and 4072). ʾAbū Bakr al-Ḥaṭṭābʾ does not appear elsewhere in WAAMD.

Name: Ibn ʿUskār, Abū al-Qāsim
Documentation: Original cataloguing attributed this work to the familiar names of two authors, both jurists, widely found in West African libraries: Ibn ʿAskar (author # 200) and Abi al-Qasim (author # 2288).

Name: Ibn al-Bārzi, Abu al-Qāsim
Documentation: Original cataloguing identified the author of this work by two familiar names: Ibn al-Barzi does not appear elsewhere in WAAMD; Abi al-Qasim is a nickname for author #2288, Khalaf b. Abī al-Qāsim Muḥammad al-Azdī.

Name: Ibn Kabīr, Abū Muḥammad
Documentation: The appellation "Kabir" appears in four familiar names in WAAMD; the most likely match for this "Ibn Kabir" is author #2564, Muḥammad Aḥmad.

Name: Ibn Nāsr al-Dīn, Shams al-Dīn
Documentation: Original cataloguing attributed two nicknames as the author of this work; WAAMD records contain two other Nāsr al-Dīn and ten Shams al-Dīn familiar names.

Name: Khāzan, Abū Jaʿfar
Documentation: Original cataloguing attributed the authorship of this work to what appear to be two nicknames; Khāzan does not appear in WAAMD; Abū Jaʿfar is found as a familiar name for authors # 2956 and # 4178.

Name: Mala ʿAṣām
Documentation: see author # 4665 for another " ʿAṣām" in the WAAMD.

Name: Shʿala
Documentation: This is the only manuscript on hadith in this collection; the attributed author has not been identified.

Name: Yahya al-Dīn, Ibn ʿArabī
Documentation: Original cataloguing provided two familiar names to the author of these works: Yahya al-Dīn which appears to refer to the grammarian, author # 1970, Ḥasan b. al-Thamalaj, and Ibn ʿArabī which appears to refer to the Sufi writer, author # 3045, Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. ʿArabī al-Ḥātimī al-Ṭāʾī

Name: Zayn al-Dīn
Documentation: Original cataloguing of these works assigned the familiar name "Zayn al-Dīn" to their author; one other Zayn al-Din in WAAMD wrote on fiqh, author # 305; another wrote on grammar, author # 6359; and none addressed Qurʾanic recitation.

Name: Zayn al-Dīn Abū al-Qāsim
Also Known As: Zayn al-Dīn Abū al-Qāsim, Jār Allāh
Documentation: Zayn al-Dīn Abū al-Qāsim, Jār Allāh are the familiar names given to the author of these works in the original catalogue. Abi al-Qasim (author # 2288) is a nickname for one widely studied authority on Maliki law found in WAAMD.  None of the five Zayn al-Din nicknames in WAAMD wrote on Qurʾanic recitation.  The name Jār Allāh here is unique in WAAMD.
